correctness.rationale: The kernel factorizes exactly under CRT because the selector multiplies prime-power congruence indicators. Unimodular row/column subtraction within polynomial-image fibers reduces each q-block to (q-1)I_s+J_s plus a zero block; no fiber-size scaling is introduced. For 1<=j<s, every j-minor is divisible by (q-1)^(j-1) and an explicit shifted minor attains the bound; the determinant gives the final divisor. Tensoring unimodular equivalences and sorting valuations gives the full Smith diagonal at arbitrary composite modulus; rank recovers each local image cardinality. Square formulas follow from exact p-adic unit-square counts. The independent, pure-stdlib checker passed 126 exact grouped tests; correctness of the infinite theorem rests on the proof, not finite computation.

value.rationale: All polynomial-value unitary-divisor difference matrices form a natural arithmetic family governed by CRT congruence equality. The result provides a complete invariant-factor formula for arbitrary modulus and polynomial, proving the polynomial local-image counts are necessary and sufficient for the entire family, although unequal fiber sizes are irrelevant; this is an arithmetically meaningful structural classification beyond one table or a substitution. The 4-adic different-fiber example proves a nontrivial invariance, and 7-torsion at modulus 15 demonstrates subtle integer behavior not predicted by modulus primes. It does not assert a novelty claim for the standard aI+J lemma or the earlier squarefree identity-polynomial case.
